editorial.headline: Electric Office Machinery With a Clear PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28172 covers the manufacture of electric and electronic office and accounting machines, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28172 is a manufacturing classification for the machines that sit behind office administration, accounting counters, mailrooms, copy desks, and document handling. The scope covers electric office and accounting machines, including electric calculators, electric typewriters, stencil machines, calculators, postage meters, mail-handling machines, stenography machines, analogue photocopiers, binding tools, coin-counting and coin-sorting machines, pencil sharpeners, staplers, voting machines, and paper punching machines. It also extends to electronic office and accounting machinery such as electronic calculating machines and cash registers.

The centre of gravity is production, not upkeep. The slim record draws the boundary around making these machines; it excludes the manufacture of electronic subassemblies and computing-machine components, and it excludes maintenance and repair services for the machines in this group. That distinction matters because KBLI 28172 is not a broad technology-services bucket. It is a factory-side code for finished office, accounting, document, coin, and related administrative machines.

The registration picture is unusually broad on scale. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can describe a small producer as well as a larger manufacturing setup. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling stated in the data, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali reading is also clear, and it should not be made more complicated than the record allows. Bali’s moratorium rule says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But for this activity, the Bali field is not marked blocked. The record’s reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is that KBLI 28172 is nationally open to PMA and, on this slim record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
